212 Men by Carolina Herrera is a Woody Floral Musk fragrance for men. 212 Men was launched in 1999. 212 Men was created by Alberto Morillas, Rosendo Mateu and Ann Gottlieb. Top notes are Green Notes, Grapefruit, Spices, Bergamot, Lavender and Petitgrain; middle notes are Ginger, Violet, Gardenia and Sage; base notes are Musk, Sandalwood, Incense, Vetiver, Guaiac Wood and Labdanum.

Jaime N 10/02/25 08:19

Perfectly adequate naming for this one. You can smell the Central Park but, somehow, you can also smell the human activity and urban comotion around it. It smells predominantly grassy, but the florals add an acidic sweetness that smells slightly funky to my nose. It does evoke a modern - in a 90's way - and cosmopolitan, casual and kind-of-clean vibe and it's still a good option for those who enjoy fresh and casual scents and want to avoid the typical blue fragrances. For my part, I find myself having a hard time choosing the right occasion to wear it. It's better suited for casual daily wear, sure, but at the same time there's this club-y aspect to it which translates to an identity crisis of sorts (I feel the same way about YSL's Myslf, though this smells more masculine). Come to think of it, this does remind of how all the metrossexual guys used to smell in the 90's/2000's nightclubs...
My girlfriend loves it though, so I wear it for her from time to time.

New batches still perform great for this type of freshie.

7.75/10

venussiandehermes 06/26/25 13:12

CH 212 Men can be considered as a work that has not received the value it deserves in the perfume world. This perfume has remained an original scent since its introduction. There is still no perfume like it today. It has an elegance that is very different from mainstream tonkali and bubble gum scents. Unfortunately, CH 212 Men, which remained in the shadow of marketing strategies, trends and "hip" brands, has remained in the background over time; most users evaluated it on the surface, thinking it was an ordinary "fresh" perfume.

However, the real power of CH 212 Men is its unique scent that does not get lost in the crowd. The freshness of green notes, the energy of spices and the balance of the woody base are so delicately constructed that it creates an air that is both sophisticated and accessible. It is neither too heavy nor simple. Especially the fact that it centers on a flower note such as gardenia, which is rarely seen in men's perfumes, is an elegant detail that distinguishes it from its peers.

Among formulas that are often either too sweet or stuck on intense masculine lines in the world of fragrances, CH 212 Men offers an alternative that is both original and balanced. Perhaps it has been overlooked because of this “middle-of-the-road elegance”, because it is not overdone. Yet it deserves appreciation and rediscovery precisely for this aspect: a perfume with character but without shouting.

In conclusion, CH 212 Men is a classic that has been appreciated late, not only by nostalgia but also by today’s standards of fragrance, and stands out for its originality and refinement. Perhaps it is time to re-appreciate its “quiet elegance”.

arno85 03/19/25 13:28

This is a fragrance I initially found intriguing but, over time, it didn't quite meet my expectations. While the scent has a fresh and energetic start, with citrus and green notes that are lively and modern, it quickly transitions to a heart and base that I personally found less appealing.

As the fragrance develops, the floral and spicy notes become more prominent, with lavender and pepper playing a significant role. However, the combination didn't resonate with me, and I felt it lacked the balance I look for in a scent. The woody and musky base, which is often the highlight of many fragrances, didn’t leave the lasting impression I had hoped for.

I did appreciate the clean and sleek design of the bottle, which mirrors the modern aesthetic of the fragrance. However, despite its popularity and reputation, the overall scent profile and its progression didn't align with my personal taste.

While I understand that 212 Men may work well for others who enjoy fresh, floral, and slightly spicy fragrances, it wasn't the right match for me. Eventually, I decided to pass it along to someone who could appreciate it more.

I'm not sure that I've ever been disappointed and impressed with a fragrance in equal measures before, but here goes...
New batch and a 100ml blind buy as going on other reviews (positive and negative), I was so utterly convinced that I would love it.
What did I think I was getting? Grass. Not vetiver. Maybe a modern, sweet, damp grass with strong supporting notes. For its faults, I love CK Truth and maybe in the back of my head I thought it would be a stronger performing version of that?

EbagAppez 03/02/25 15:56

212 Men is a classic mens fragrance that was released back in 1999. The fact that it is still being sold today speaks volumes about how good it still is.

I originally purchased my first bottle back in 2004, and I just recently purchased a new 50ml last summer (2024). I can honestly say, this has not seen any notable change in the scent profile, or even the performance 20+ years later! This current bottle smells and performs just the way I remember my original bottle!

The performance is still great on me especially for a fresh style fragrance. I easily get 8 hours of solid active performance before it dies down to a skin scent by the 9/10 hour mark. From a projection standpoint, it pops off my skin at an arms length for a good 4 hours and leaves a good sillage trail during that span of time.

I sprayed one pump on my forearm last night and it was still wafting up to my nose for 4 hours until I went to bed. The next morning I could still smell it on my forearm when I got in the shower after my morning workout. Granted, it was a skin scent at that point, but I could still smell it on my arm, so this stuff just sticks to my skin.

212 is well balanced with some citrus and is very fresh smelling, you can really smell the green in this which makes it perfect for day wear and works well for the Spring. It’s not too heavy on the citrus and is quite refined and sophisticated, with very slight woody notes coming through giving it a small masculine kick.

If you’re looking for something for the Spring or Summer and you come across this, you’ll want to give it a try.

While this is now considered a classic/older men's scent, I think many open minded younger buyers can appreciate this one if they are getting tired of smelling the endless array of cotton candy and pixie dust style scents filling the current marketplace.

This is a long lasting timeless fragrance objectively, but with a big twist in my experience...

Okay these are all the good stuff I talked about, now here comes the plot twist
Subjectively, this fragrance is literally unwearable
I've heard im not the only one experiencing this phenomenon, but whenever I smell a fragrance that contains the Sandalwood note in it I instantly get nausea. I'm close to vomiting whenever I smell the opening of this perfume and I can't help it.

Carolina Herrera 212 Men: I was understood enough in what I've said above, objectively it's a sexy grassy scent around 8.25/10. And for me due to my experience this can't get anything above a 4-5/10 since its unwearable. The bottle is the star of the show, MUST 100% try before you buy

A perfume that speaks itself.
An Awesome creation by Alberto Morillas in collaboration with Rosendo Mateu and Ann Gottlieb

It is an all-rounder, best suited for the fall and winter, but wearable through the spring. I wouldn't recommend it for the summer, given its musk can be overwhelming for the user (at least it is for me). I consider it a pretty decent signature scent, and easy to wear for most people. Works well in an office environment, so long you control your sprays, night outs and casual scenarios. Even though it's not particularly sexy, in my experience, women tend to really like it, so it can work as a date scent, if you only have a couple fragrances. There are, of course, better suited frags for that purpose, all I'm saying is it can work well in dates too. Like I said, I do not recommend it for hot summer days, though.
It is a very particular scent, reminiscent of fresh cut grass, so it has a very good memory effect. People will recognise and identify it with little to no effort.

Longevity: 8.5/10
Projection and Sillage: 7/10
Fragrance Quality: 8/10
Value for money: 8/10

If you have performance issues; make sure you buy from a trusted source

Giving a thought about 212 Men for the last years through all my designer fragrance journey and all the scents I've put my nose on it, I've come to the conclusion that to me this is one of the most underrated designer fragrance I've ever come across. Yeah, you read it. Now you can hate on me or whatever you want. You might think I'm exaggerating or something. Not at all.

It gives you basically everything you can ask for a signature-worthy fragrance. It gives off all-year round versatility and some uniqueness which if you think about it, it is REALLY hard having those 2 at once. That's not very common in a signature scent. There's not many perfumes out there that smell like 212 or at least very close to it and its scent profile hasn't been overused over the years. Also, it has complexity. It has projection. It has longevity. It has sillage. It's a compliment magnet and it costs a fair price. Only drawbacks you might consider:
A. It still sells after 20+ years and therefore it might end up being somewhat "popular" or "familiar".
B. It might not smell as high-quality as Dior or Chanel. But at the end of the day, you get what you pay for in that regard and that's just a fact.

Having mentioned all of this, As I said previously, it's among the most underrated scents in the designer realm. It definitely deserves way more love and recognition. Nobody in the fragrance community ever talks about it for some reason. I guess it is because it's Carolina Herrera. This community is full of snobbish and pretentious people who think they know something. If this were Chanel every single one of them would praise the f out of it for centuries. 212 is not worse than the overpraised Bleu de Chanel.

10/10 Masterpiece. Best well-balanced designer perfume. My compatriot Alberto Morillas did a superb job with 212 Men

Contrary to voting, citrus is not dominant. This fragrance will make you feel sporty and a little luxurious. It is suitable for men under the average age of 35.

I'm pretty sure it's "Turkish Tea" from one of the notes described as green notes. (For those who do not know the smell of Turkish tea) It is an aromatic scent that comes out when bergamot peel and exotic green leaves are dried. The scent has a tea scent, which makes it unique.

I feel a fresh and slightly spicy scent. Spices are similar to rosemary and ginger spice. It's a refreshing spice that's not irritating. At the bottom, there is a smoky vanilla scent.

The fragrance is generally aromatic, sugary and slightly spicy. It is quite unique. It's hard to come across an imitation.

It stays on fabric for more than 8 hours. It stays on the skin for up to 4 hours. The projection and sillage ratio is not bad.

Fragrance Quality: 8/10

The deeper you get into fragrances, the more you find what fits or works best for you. There was a time when this was in my top five fragrances. Perhaps as the years go by one's tastes may deviate a bit, or your body chemistry changes. CH 212 Men is really a classy signature-worthy fragrance. But it's one I am leaving behind.

I no longer enjoy that grassy, fresh scent as much as I did. Wearing this recently made me see how "synthetic" a fragrance it is. I don't say this often but it gave me a headache wearing it, and I felt like it made its way to the back of my throat. Quite uncomfortable. The dry-down settled into something reminiscent of strong body odour at times, and it got me wondering if people around me were smelling this as well. I hope they weren't. God, I hope!

Despite my recent disappointment CH 212 Men gets top marks for what I remember it to be. This fragrance gave me some unforgettable memories, and transports me to a more carefree time of my life. Please don't be discouraged by my recent experience with 212 Men. It's not the fragrance, it is me. I have changed - I'd like to think for the better. This legendary fragrance played a starring role in my life, and I hope it will in yours, too.

At first, I really didn't like this fragrance much at all. However, after wearing it a little, it really has started to grow on me!

The opening is a little harsh if you're not expecting it. Fragrantica lists this as a citrus fragrance, but the green notes are most prominent for me. Since it caught me off-guard, it almost reminded me of... grass. However, it really grew on me and it's a lot more pleasant than my first impression.

As it progresses into the mids and base notes, it settles really nicely! The citrus dies down, and the spices and musky notes come out, giving off a certain city vibe to it. I've never been to New York, but this fragrance definitely makes me think of the Bay Area, the BART train, and the fog in the summertime.

This fragrance is definitely really summery, fresh, retro, and energizing. Throughout hotter months I could definitely use this as a dumb reach. It really gives off that 90's GQ attitude!

This fragrance has average performance with like 5-6 hours, which is about all you need to ask of it. Considering it's strictly a daytime fragrance, something for after the gym or something before a nice meeting, it's nice for it not to linger too long and make way for a night out fragrance.

overall, it's a good fragrance. Blind buy safe in my opinion. If you don't like it, you know someone who does. 4/5

Deswizard 03/08/21 00:01

I was with a friend when they bought this in 2012, right around the time Azealia Banks song '212' was released. I thought they were related. They're not, thank goodness.

This scent is citrus and green right from the onset, with just a smudge of lavender to smooth down the bite from the citrus. I don't pick up any spice notes at all.

In the dry-down I get the flower notes, which add an even deeper sense of being in a meadow or a glade, and just the faintest hintof ginger.

When this bottoms out, which takes a while, the wood notes, particularly the sandalwood, come properly into existence.

Throughout the life of this perfume the citrus and lavender never disappear, which makes this a perfect scent for hot climates and sunny days. I find it a little too fresh for Autumn, though. I would call this 'buoyant' and 'juicy'.

This is definitely a scent for men from their early 20' s to early 30's. You can wear this to the office or the gym or out for errands or meetings. Definitely grab this if you don't know what to wear. 212 is a bit too common now to ever be considered niche, but you'll never go wrong with it.

Projection is strong, sillage is moderate and it easily lasts the whole day.

I've already reviewed 212 before, but my review was based on the original (pre-reformulation) version.
Last week I got my hands on a new bottle (a 2019 batch manufactured by Puig), first of all the box has changed, the name is now "212 MEN NYC" instead of "212 MEN" on the old box, the bottle itself is much lighter and of slightly cheaper quality than the old one.

Performance wise, the longevity is still very good, it will last you the whole day without any issues, the projection is definately much more weaker than the old formulation, after about 1-2 hours it will start sitting closer to the skin than it used to be.

alexvpm 11/01/23 02:12

Giving a thought about 212 Men for the last years through all my designer fragrance journey and all the scents I've put my nose on it, I've come to the conclusion that to me this is one of the most underrated designer fragrance I've ever come across. Yeah, you read it. Now you can hate on me or whatever you want. You might think I'm exaggerating or something. Not at all.

It gives you basically everything you can ask for a signature-worthy fragrance. It gives off all-year round versatility and some uniqueness which if you think about it, it is REALLY hard having those 2 at once. That's not very common in a signature scent. There's not many perfumes out there that smell like 212 or at least very close to it and its scent profile hasn't been overused over the years. Also, it has complexity. It has projection. It has longevity. It has sillage. It's a compliment magnet and it costs a fair price. Only drawbacks you might consider:
A. It still sells after 20+ years and therefore it might end up being somewhat "popular" or "familiar".
B. It might not smell as high-quality as Dior or Chanel. But at the end of the day, you get what you pay for in that regard and that's just a fact.

Having mentioned all of this, As I said previously, it's among the most underrated scents in the designer realm. It definitely deserves way more love and recognition. Nobody in the fragrance community ever talks about it for some reason. I guess it is because it's Carolina Herrera. This community is full of snobbish and pretentious people who think they know something. If this were Chanel every single one of them would praise the f out of it for centuries. 212 is not worse than the overpraised Bleu de Chanel.

10/10 Masterpiece. Best well-balanced designer perfume. My compatriot Alberto Morillas did a superb job with 212 Men
